audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart and the content-layer level chart disagree on the last two rows: phases[5].side is 'Sylas' while win[5] is 'Aurelion Sol', and phases[6].side is 'Skill' while win[6] is 'Aurelion Sol'. Both phases[5].why and phases[6].why describe Aurelion Sol winning those stages, so the full-layer side contradicts its own why as well.
audit.why: Both layers' prose already agree that the first item and 2+ items belong to Aurelion Sol (E executes the wave, Q burn outranges Sylas's 775 Chain Lash and 400-unit Abscond). Only the side token was stale.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and phases[6].side both set to 'Aurelion Sol', matching win[5]/win[6] which already read 'Aurelion Sol'. No why rewrite needed — both whys already describe Aurelion Sol winning.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is attributed to the passive: whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid and wants.foe[0] all say 'Petricite Burst' gives him a free ultimate / heal-reset. The packet flags this as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: Petricite Burst (P) is a spell-cast charge that whirls his chains on the next basic attack and grants attack speed. The ultimate steal is Hijack (R), 80/55/30s. The sustain is Kingslayer (W), 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s. Three different abilities were collapsed into the passive's name.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike restated as Hijack (R) on an 80-second cooldown at rank 1, dropping to 30s at rank 3, stealing Falling Star and turning your only self-peel stun into his engage tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of this matchup — Hijack stealing Falling Star / The Skies Descend — is never stated. Separately, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t all describe Abscond / Abduct as a 'dash into chain-stun'; Abduct pulls Sylas to the target and applies no stun. Sylas has no hard CC of his own anywhere in his kit.
audit.why: Abscond (E) dashes 400 units and the Abduct recast throws chains to pull him to an enemy hit — displacement of himself, not a stun on you. Aurelion Sol's Q is an interruptible channel, and nothing in Sylas's own kit interrupts it; only a hijacked ultimate can. Chain Lash (Q, 775) slightly outranges your Breath of Light (750). Kingslayer (W) heals against champions, so Grievous Wounds decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers (E 13/12/11/10/9, W 12→6, R 80/55/30), in report[5].t (400-unit dash then recast pull, 13s at rank 1), and the Hijack-steals-Falling-Star interaction written into whys[4], spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all — the one field that is supposed to hold real cooldowns.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 3. Every number needed is in the kit.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Abscond/Abduct 13s at rank 1 to 9s at rank 5, Kingslayer 12s to 6s, Hijack 80/55/30.

audit.why: Defect catalogue item 7, plus the needs-antiheal missing interaction.
audit.corrected: late now names Liandry's, Rabadon's and Zhonya's and keeps anti-heal against Kingslayer; ahead front-loads the anti-heal buy.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer still describes the pre-rework Aurelion Sol: 'your short-range star poke', 'your stars', 'star size', 'max star stacks', and an 'R shred-and-knockback beam' plus a 'stun-detonate combo' that do not exist in the current kit.
audit.why: Current kit: Q Breath of Light is a 750-range channelled beam, E is a black hole with a percent-health execute, R is Falling Star (stun) upgrading to The Skies Descend. There are no orbiting stars and no detonate.
audit.corrected: whys[0], spikes[0].text, spikes[3].text and late rewritten in current-kit language (750 beam, stardust bank, Falling Star / The Skies Descend).

edits.before: Sylas
edits.after: Aurelion Sol

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Aurelion Sol

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Sylas wins by Abducting you mid-channel, healing it back with Kingslayer (W), then hijacking your Falling Star to stun you with it.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Astral Flight spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Abscond/Abduct (E): 13s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — the recast pull is his only gap-close, so step up the moment it is spent. - Kingslayer (W) is 12s down to 6s and heals him; anti-heal decides long trades. - Hijack (R): 80/55/30 — rank 3 re-steals every 30s.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by outranging him: Sylas has one 775-range tool in Chain Lash (Q) and must walk into your Q beam to do anything, so stardust and range decide it.

edits.before: If Sylas takes first blood, tighten up: Abscond / Abduct is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with E executes and stay relevant through the stardust curve.
edits.after: If Sylas takes first blood, his Hijack is now a second ultimate aimed at you every 80 seconds. A second kill and the duel is finished — farm the wave with E executes from max range and bank stardust instead of contesting.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Sylas on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, buy anti-heal early so Kingslayer stops refilling him, then take every W flyby the moment his E is on its 13-second cooldown and deny him the side lane entirely.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Abscond (E) covers 400 units and Abduct pulls him the rest — a tower freeze keeps that recast out of range.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Sylas for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: Falling Star's stun is your only answer to an Abduct that lands — keep it for his commit, not for a wave, and Flash out if you eat both dashes.

edits.before: Sylas whiffs Abscond / Abduct and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Hijack makes his roams worth double — ward before he leaves, not after.

edits.before: That is Sylas’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Inside 775 he answers with Chain Lash and closes on the slow — beam at max range only.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: He clears with Chain Lash and heals the chip back with Kingslayer, so a shove contest just hands him the wave and your health bar.

edits.before: Track Sylas’s Abscond / Abduct: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Abscond / Abduct: he dashes 400 units, then recasts to chain himself onto you. It is 13s at rank 1 — that window is your green light.

edits.before: Level 1: Sylas's Q-E poke and Petricite Burst sustain already out-trade your short-range star poke.
edits.after: Level 1: Chain Lash outranges your 750 beam and Petricite Burst's whirl punishes you the moment he steps in.

edits.before: Level 6: Petricite Burst gives him a free reset or a stolen ultimate, letting him force fights on his terms.
edits.after: Level 6: Hijack steals your Falling Star, so he holds a stun on an 80-second cooldown and you hold none.

edits.before: Sylas hits his Q-E all-in the moment he has 3 points down and simply walks through your stars — you have no stun up in time to stop it.
edits.after: At 3 points Sylas has Chain Lash to slow, Abscond to close and Kingslayer to heal the trade back — and your R does not exist yet to stop any of it.

edits.before: Petricite Burst gives him a free ultimate to reset the trade or steal one of yours off a nearby wave, snowballing the all-in even harder.
edits.after: Hijack (R) takes your Falling Star and casts it at you for free — the stun you were saving as self-peel now opens his all-in instead.

edits.before: With full stacks and a completed core you outrange and out-burst him from a screen away — he can't jump onto you without dying to the stun-detonate combo first.
edits.after: With deep stardust and a completed core the Q burn out-damages anything he heals back — and any Abduct onto you eats Falling Star before Kingslayer can refill him.

edits.before: Level 6 is the danger point: Sylas can steal an ultimate off a nearby laner or just use Petricite Burst's free heal-reset to renew his all-in, so expect a dive attempt the moment he hits it. Keep your Q on cooldown-watch and try to land a stun before he closes the gap rather than after. Ward your flanks since he loves to roam off deep wards and duel side-lane targets with his stolen ultimate. If you can survive to your first completed item without dying twice, the lane starts turning — his damage plateaus while your star size and Q range keep scaling.
edits.after: Level 6 is the danger point, but the ability to fear is Hijack (R), not the passive: he steals your Falling Star and holds your own stun on an 80-second cooldown, so treat every level-6 step forward as if you have no ultimate at all. Ward your flanks — a stolen ultimate makes his roams and side-lane duels far stronger than his own kit. Keep Astral Flight (W) banked as the escape and never spend it poking. If you reach your first completed item without dying twice the lane turns: his damage plateaus while your stardust total and Q burn keep climbing.

edits.before: With a full item build and max star stacks you completely outrange him — Q hits from well outside his E gap-close distance, and your R shred-and-knockback beam punishes any dive attempt before he's even in melee range. He has no ranged answer, so as long as you don't get caught out of position by flanking assassins, you can poke and burst him down safely in every teamfight. Build burst/range items (Luden's-style, Shadowflame) rather than defensive stats — the goal is to end fights before he ever reaches you.
edits.after: With a full build and a deep stardust bank you simply outrange him — the Q beam reaches 750 while his Abscond dash covers 400, so he must burn E and the Abduct recast just to touch you. Falling Star, or The Skies Descend once you have the stardust for it, is the answer to that jump: stun him out of the air and burn him down while he is still airborne. Build Liandry's and Rabadon's into Zhonya's, and keep anti-heal so Kingslayer cannot buy him a second attempt at you.

edits.before: Force all-ins at level 3 and again at 6 with Petricite Burst up
edits.after: Force all-ins at level 3, then hijack your Falling Star at 6

notes:
KIT FLAG MISFIRE: ownerKit W (Astral Flight) carries the derived flag terrain='creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Riot's own description says Aurelion Sol FLIES OVER terrain — it creates nothing. The missingInteractions entry 'enemy-dash-deniable: Your Astral Flight (W) shuts off Sylas's Kingslayer (W), Abscond/Abduct (E)' is built on that bad flag and is FALSE. I did not write it anywhere; the rule-generator should be corrected or this headline will reach other Aurelion Sol matchups. The needs-antiheal interaction is real and is now in ahead and late.

TWO-LAYER CHART DISAGREEMENT FOUND AND FIXED: phases[5].side ('Sylas') vs win[5] ('Aurelion Sol') and phases[6].side ('Skill') vs win[6] ('Aurelion Sol'). Only the full layer needed moving; win[5]/win[6] were already correct so no content edit was required for the pair. Both phases whys already described Aurelion Sol winning, so no why rewrite was needed to keep row and sentence in agreement.

Did not touch phases[0..4] — packet.levelChart, both layers and the prose all agree Sylas owns levels 1-5, which is consistent with a scaling matchup at 50.39% over 1284 games.

UNVERIFIED / LEFT ALONE: whether Sylas's hijacked Falling Star can ever be the upgraded The Skies Descend, and whether Aurelion Sol's Q channel is broken by Chain Lash's slow (the kit flags Q as 'interruptible — any CC cancels it' but does not say whether a slow counts). Nothing in the kits answers either, so no text asserts either way.
